I will keep my full 4.5 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because my land is small, I have well irrigation, and after 35 years of farming I trust a stable double-cropping system more than taking risks. I will use better-performing seed on both crops to protect yield on limited land. For winter wheat, I will push steady fertilization and a few irrigations, because wheat here responds well to water and nitrogen if I want reliable grain filling. I will use rotary tillage after maize harvest to prepare a fine seedbed and keep field work efficient. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed after wheat, keep fertilizer balanced but with less irrigation than wheat, and use fewer pesticide sprays unless pressure rises, because maize is usually stronger and the season is warmer and faster. Since some family members work off-farm, I will keep the plan practical and input-efficient rather than overly labor-intensive.
